cards.front: What are the two hallmark lesions of Alzheimer disease, and where is each one found?
cards.back: **Amyloid-β plaques**: extracellular, made from cleavage of **amyloid precursor protein (APP)**. **Neurofibrillary tangles**: intracellular, made of **hyperphosphorylated tau**; tangle burden tracks with dementia severity. Grossly: cortical atrophy with wide sulci, worst in the **hippocampus**.
cards.back_pt: **Placas de amiloide-β**: extracelulares, formadas pela clivagem da **proteína precursora do amiloide (APP)**. **Emaranhados neurofibrilares**: intracelulares, formados por **tau hiperfosforilada**; a quantidade de emaranhados acompanha a gravidade da demência. Macroscopia: atrofia cortical com sulcos alargados, mais intensa no **hipocampo**.

cards.front: Which genes are linked to early-onset and to late-onset Alzheimer disease?
cards.back: Early onset (autosomal dominant): **APP** (chromosome 21), **presenilin-1** and **presenilin-2**. Late onset: **APOE ε4** raises risk; ε2 is protective. The extra APP copy in **Down syndrome** brings the brain changes of Alzheimer early, usually by about age 40; dementia often follows later.
cards.back_pt: Início precoce (autossômico dominante): **APP** (cromossomo 21), **presenilina-1** e **presenilina-2**. Início tardio: o **APOE ε4** aumenta o risco; o ε2 é protetor. A cópia extra do APP na **síndrome de Down** antecipa as alterações cerebrais de Alzheimer, em geral por volta dos 40 anos; a demência costuma surgir mais tarde.

cards.front: A 58-year-old has new disinhibition, apathy and poor judgment, but memory is fairly intact. What is the likely dementia, and what inclusions may be seen?
cards.back: **Frontotemporal dementia**: atrophy of the frontal and temporal lobes, with early **behavior** or **language** change and memory spared at first. Inclusions are often **tau** (round **Pick bodies**) or **TDP-43**.
cards.back_pt: **Demência frontotemporal**: atrofia dos lobos frontais e temporais, com alteração precoce do **comportamento** ou da **linguagem** e memória preservada no início. As inclusões costumam ser de **tau** (**corpúsculos de Pick**, arredondados) ou de **TDP-43**.

cards.front: Which features point to Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease?
cards.back: **Rapidly progressive dementia** (weeks to months) with **startle myoclonus**. Misfolded **prion protein** (β-sheet form) converts normal prion protein. The brain shows **spongiform change** without inflammation. EEG may show periodic sharp waves; CSF may show **14-3-3 protein**.
cards.back_pt: **Demência rapidamente progressiva** (semanas a meses) com **mioclonias desencadeadas por sobressalto**. A **proteína priônica** mal dobrada (forma em folha β) converte a proteína priônica normal. O cérebro mostra **alteração espongiforme** sem inflamação. O EEG pode mostrar ondas agudas periódicas; o LCR pode mostrar **proteína 14-3-3**.

cards.front: What is the core pathology of Parkinson disease?
cards.back: Loss of **dopaminergic neurons** in the **substantia nigra pars compacta** (pale nigra on gross exam), so nigrostriatal dopamine falls. Surviving neurons contain **Lewy bodies**: eosinophilic inclusions of **α-synuclein**. Signs: resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability.
cards.back_pt: Perda de **neurônios dopaminérgicos** da **substância negra parte compacta** (despigmentação da substância negra à macroscopia), com queda da dopamina nigroestriatal. Os neurônios restantes contêm **corpúsculos de Lewy**: inclusões eosinofílicas de **α-sinucleína**. Sinais: tremor de repouso, rigidez, bradicinesia, instabilidade postural.

cards.front: Which pattern of findings defines amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)?
cards.back: Both **upper motor neuron** signs (spasticity, hyperreflexia, Babinski) and **lower motor neuron** signs (atrophy, fasciculations), with **sensation spared**. Some familial cases have **SOD1** mutations. **Riluzole** lowers glutamate release and modestly prolongs survival.
cards.back_pt: Sinais de **neurônio motor superior** (espasticidade, hiper-reflexia, Babinski) e de **neurônio motor inferior** (atrofia, fasciculações), com **sensibilidade preservada**. Alguns casos familiares têm mutação do **SOD1**. O **riluzol** reduz a liberação de glutamato e prolonga modestamente a sobrevida.

cards.front: What is the mechanism of myasthenia gravis, and how does the weakness behave?
cards.back: Antibodies against the postsynaptic **acetylcholine receptor** (type II hypersensitivity). **Fatigable weakness**: ptosis and diplopia that worsen with use and improve with rest; an **ice pack** on the eyelid improves ptosis. Linked to **thymoma** and **thymic hyperplasia**.
cards.back_pt: Anticorpos contra o **receptor de acetilcolina** pós-sináptico (hipersensibilidade tipo II). **Fraqueza com fatigabilidade**: ptose e diplopia que pioram com o uso e melhoram com o repouso; **gelo** sobre a pálpebra melhora a ptose. Associada a **timoma** e **hiperplasia tímica**.

cards.front: Which virus causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), and in which patients?
cards.back: Reactivation of **JC virus**, which infects and kills **oligodendrocytes**, causing patchy demyelination. Seen with severe immunosuppression: **AIDS**, transplant, and drugs such as **natalizumab** or **rituximab**. Rapid, often fatal decline.
cards.back_pt: Reativação do **vírus JC**, que infecta e destrói **oligodendrócitos**, causando desmielinização em focos esparsos. Ocorre em imunossupressão grave: **AIDS**, transplante e medicamentos como **natalizumabe** ou **rituximabe**. Declínio rápido, muitas vezes fatal.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man is brought in by his wife because of 10 months of problems with attention and memory. His alertness changes a lot from day to day; on some days he seems almost normal. He often describes seeing small children in the house who are not there. Over the same period, he has developed slow movements and mild rigidity in both arms. Last month, a short course of haloperidol for agitation made his rigidity much worse and increased his confusion. Which finding is most likely at autopsy?
choices: Spongiform vacuoles in the cortex with abnormal prion protein
Multiple small lacunar infarcts in the deep white matter
α-Synuclein inclusions in cortical and brainstem neurons
Round tau inclusions in neurons of the frontal and temporal lobes
Amyloid-β plaques and tau tangles that begin in the hippocampus
questions.explanation: **Fluctuating cognition**, well-formed **visual hallucinations**, parkinsonism that starts with or soon after the dementia, and severe **sensitivity to antipsychotics** point to **Lewy body dementia**. Its lesion is the **Lewy body**, an **α-synuclein** inclusion in cortical and brainstem neurons. Alzheimer disease is the most tempting choice, but it starts with steady memory loss; early hallucinations, day-to-day fluctuation and parkinsonism are not typical.
questions.explanation_pt: **Cognição flutuante**, **alucinações visuais** bem formadas, parkinsonismo que começa junto ou logo após a demência e grande **sensibilidade aos antipsicóticos** indicam **demência com corpúsculos de Lewy**. A lesão é o **corpúsculo de Lewy**, uma inclusão de **α-sinucleína** em neurônios corticais e do tronco encefálico. A doença de Alzheimer é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas começa com perda de memória progressiva; alucinações precoces, flutuação diária e parkinsonismo não são típicos.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man is evaluated for 1 year of restlessness, poor concentration and sudden, brief, irregular movements of his face and fingers that flow from one body part to another. His father first showed similar movements at age 50. MRI shows atrophy of the caudate nuclei. Genetic testing confirms the diagnosis. Which mechanism best explains why this patient's disease began earlier than his father's?
choices: Genomic imprinting of the paternal allele
Incomplete penetrance of the mutant allele
Variable expressivity caused by environmental factors
Germline mosaicism in the father
Expansion of a CAG trinucleotide repeat during spermatogenesis
questions.explanation: This is **Huntington disease**: autosomal dominant **CAG repeat** expansion in the huntingtin gene (*HTT*) on **chromosome 4**, with **caudate atrophy** and chorea. Longer repeats cause earlier onset, and the repeat is unstable and tends to grow in the **male germline**, so onset moves earlier in the next generation (**anticipation**). Variable expressivity is tempting, but it describes different severity with the same mutation, not a repeat that grows from one generation to the next.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se da **doença de Huntington**: expansão autossômica dominante de **repetições CAG** no gene da huntingtina (*HTT*), no **cromossomo 4**, com **atrofia do caudado** e coreia. Repetições maiores causam início mais precoce, e a repetição é instável e tende a crescer na **linhagem germinativa masculina**, por isso o início fica mais precoce na geração seguinte (**antecipação**). A expressividade variável é tentadora, mas descreve gravidade diferente com a mesma mutação, e não uma repetição que cresce de uma geração para a outra.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has 3 days of double vision. Two years ago, she had pain with eye movement and blurred vision in her right eye that resolved over 6 weeks. When she looks to the right, her left eye does not adduct and her right eye shows nystagmus. Convergence is normal. She also has tingling in her legs that gets worse after a hot shower. MRI shows several ovoid white matter lesions next to the lateral ventricles. Which cerebrospinal fluid finding is most likely?
choices: High protein with a normal cell count as the only abnormality
Oligoclonal IgG bands that are not present in the serum
Neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose
Xanthochromia from red blood cell breakdown
High 14-3-3 protein with a normal cell count
questions.explanation: Past **optic neuritis**, a left **internuclear ophthalmoplegia** (medial longitudinal fasciculus lesion), heat-sensitive symptoms (**Uhthoff phenomenon**) and **periventricular** plaques in a young woman indicate **multiple sclerosis**. Clonal plasma cells inside the CNS make IgG, seen as **oligoclonal bands** in the CSF but not in the serum. The most tempting distractor, high protein with normal cells (**albuminocytologic dissociation**), is typical of Guillain-Barré syndrome, a peripheral demyelinating disease without brain lesions.
questions.explanation_pt: **Neurite óptica** prévia, **oftalmoplegia internuclear** esquerda (lesão do fascículo longitudinal medial), sintomas que pioram com o calor (**fenômeno de Uhthoff**) e placas **periventriculares** em mulher jovem indicam **esclerose múltipla**. Plasmócitos clonais dentro do SNC produzem IgG, vista como **bandas oligoclonais** no LCR, mas não no soro. O distrator mais tentador, proteína alta com celularidade normal (**dissociação albuminocitológica**), é típico da síndrome de Guillain-Barré, uma doença desmielinizante periférica sem lesões encefálicas.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has 5 days of tingling in her feet and weakness that started in her legs and now involves her arms. Ten days ago, she had bloody diarrhea after eating undercooked chicken. Exam shows symmetric weakness, absent deep tendon reflexes and mild loss of sensation in the feet. Her heart rate varies between 48/min and 130/min, and her blood pressure is labile. Cerebrospinal fluid shows protein 160 mg/dL (normal 15-45) and 2 white blood cells/μL. What is the most likely mechanism of her weakness?
choices: Antibodies against the postsynaptic acetylcholine receptor
T-cell-mediated destruction of central nervous system myelin
Antibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels
Antibodies against peripheral nerve gangliosides through molecular mimicry
Degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons
questions.explanation: Ascending weakness with **areflexia** weeks after **Campylobacter jejuni** enteritis, **autonomic instability** and **albuminocytologic dissociation** indicate **Guillain-Barré syndrome**. Bacterial surface molecules resemble nerve **gangliosides**, so the immune response attacks peripheral nerve myelin or axons. Lambert-Eaton syndrome (anti-presynaptic calcium channel) also lowers reflexes, but it spares sensation, does not raise CSF protein, and strength improves with repeated effort.
questions.explanation_pt: Fraqueza ascendente com **arreflexia** semanas após enterite por **Campylobacter jejuni**, **instabilidade autonômica** e **dissociação albuminocitológica** indicam **síndrome de Guillain-Barré**. Moléculas da superfície da bactéria se parecem com **gangliosídeos** do nervo, e a resposta imune ataca a mielina ou os axônios dos nervos periféricos. A síndrome de Lambert-Eaton (anticorpos contra canais de cálcio pré-sinápticos) também reduz os reflexos, mas poupa a sensibilidade, não eleva a proteína do LCR, e a força melhora com o esforço repetido.

notes.title: Neurodegenerative and demyelinating disease: dementias, movement disorders, MS and the neuromuscular junction
notes.body_md:
## Dementias

- **Alzheimer**: amyloid-β plaques, tau tangles and **low acetylcholine** (loss of neurons in the nucleus basalis of Meynert). Memory loss comes first.
- **Frontotemporal**: behavior or language change first; tau (**Pick bodies**) or TDP-43.
- **Lewy body dementia**: α-synuclein; **fluctuating cognition**, **visual hallucinations**, parkinsonism, severe sensitivity to antipsychotics.
- **Creutzfeldt-Jakob**: prion; rapid course, **myoclonus**, spongiform change.
- Vascular dementia and normal pressure hydrocephalus: see the cerebrovascular and neuroanatomy blocks.

## Movement disorders

- **Parkinson**: loss of nigral dopamine neurons, Lewy bodies; resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, postural instability.
- **Huntington**: autosomal dominant **CAG repeat** in *HTT* (chromosome 4); **caudate atrophy**, chorea, depression, dementia; **anticipation**, mainly through the father.
- **Essential tremor**: action and postural tremor, often familial, eased by alcohol; no rigidity or bradykinesia.
- Wilson disease (liver block) and tardive dyskinesia (antipsychotics and metoclopramide) are covered elsewhere.

## CNS demyelination

- **Multiple sclerosis**: mostly young women; usually relapsing-remitting; **periventricular** plaques; **optic neuritis**, **internuclear ophthalmoplegia**, CSF **oligoclonal bands**; heat worsens symptoms (**Uhthoff phenomenon**).
- **Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis**: one episode of multifocal demyelination after an infection or vaccine, mostly in children.
- **PML**: JC virus in immunosuppressed patients.
- Osmotic demyelination: see the electrolytes block.

## Peripheral nerve and motor neuron

- **Guillain-Barré**: ascending weakness and areflexia weeks after an infection (**Campylobacter**); **albuminocytologic dissociation**; autonomic instability and respiratory failure are the dangers.
- **ALS**: upper plus lower motor neuron signs, no sensory loss; SOD1. Spinal muscular atrophy (lower motor neuron only, infants): see the spinal cord block. **Friedreich ataxia**: GAA repeat in frataxin, ataxia, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

## Neuromuscular junction

- **Myasthenia gravis**: anti-acetylcholine receptor (postsynaptic); weakness **worsens with use**; thymoma or thymic hyperplasia.
- **Lambert-Eaton**: anti-presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channel; strength **improves with use**, low reflexes, dry mouth; small cell lung cancer (respiratory block).
notes.body_pt_md:
## Demências

- **Alzheimer**: placas de amiloide-β, emaranhados de tau e **acetilcolina baixa** (perda de neurônios do núcleo basal de Meynert). A perda de memória vem primeiro.
- **Frontotemporal**: alteração do comportamento ou da linguagem primeiro; tau (**corpúsculos de Pick**) ou TDP-43.
- **Demência com corpúsculos de Lewy**: α-sinucleína; **cognição flutuante**, **alucinações visuais**, parkinsonismo, grande sensibilidade aos antipsicóticos.
- **Creutzfeldt-Jakob**: príon; evolução rápida, **mioclonia**, alteração espongiforme.
- Demência vascular e hidrocefalia de pressão normal: ver os blocos cerebrovascular e de neuroanatomia.

## Distúrbios do movimento

- **Parkinson**: perda de neurônios dopaminérgicos da substância negra, corpúsculos de Lewy; tremor de repouso, rigidez, bradicinesia, instabilidade postural.
- **Huntington**: **repetição CAG** autossômica dominante no *HTT* (cromossomo 4); **atrofia do caudado**, coreia, depressão, demência; **antecipação**, principalmente pela via paterna.
- **Tremor essencial**: tremor de ação e postural, muitas vezes familiar, que melhora com álcool; sem rigidez nem bradicinesia.
- Doença de Wilson (bloco de fígado) e discinesia tardia (antipsicóticos e metoclopramida) são tratadas em outros blocos.

## Desmielinização do SNC

- **Esclerose múltipla**: principalmente mulheres jovens; em geral remitente-recorrente; placas **periventriculares**; **neurite óptica**, **oftalmoplegia internuclear**, **bandas oligoclonais** no LCR; o calor piora os sintomas (**fenômeno de Uhthoff**).
- **Encefalomielite disseminada aguda**: episódio único de desmielinização multifocal após infecção ou vacina, principalmente em crianças.
- **LEMP**: vírus JC em imunossuprimidos.
- Desmielinização osmótica: ver o bloco de eletrólitos.

## Nervo periférico e neurônio motor

- **Guillain-Barré**: fraqueza ascendente e arreflexia semanas após uma infecção (**Campylobacter**); **dissociação albuminocitológica**; instabilidade autonômica e insuficiência respiratória são os perigos.
- **ELA**: sinais de neurônio motor superior e inferior, sem perda sensitiva; SOD1. Atrofia muscular espinhal (só neurônio motor inferior, lactentes): ver o bloco de medula espinhal. **Ataxia de Friedreich**: repetição GAA no gene da frataxina, ataxia, cardiomiopatia hipertrófica.

## Junção neuromuscular

- **Miastenia gravis**: anticorpos contra o receptor de acetilcolina (pós-sináptico); a fraqueza **piora com o uso**; timoma ou hiperplasia tímica.
- **Lambert-Eaton**: anticorpos contra o canal de cálcio voltagem-dependente pré-sináptico; a força **melhora com o uso**, reflexos reduzidos, boca seca; câncer de pulmão de pequenas células (bloco respiratório).
